goal: Resolve QA security and robustness findings in the Pros CLI, release automation, archive extraction, networking, and CI pipeline.

included: Command-injection fixes in Windows hiding logic
npm token handling improvements during publish
Network timeout, pagination, and streaming improvements
Install/update staging and version comparison robustness
excluded: Feature work unrelated to QA findings

constraints: Make the smallest correct security fixes first.
Do not change persisted runtime behavior unless required for safety.
Keep compatibility for existing auth config where possible.
Every P0 security fix must have a regression test.

tasks.title: Fix command injection in Windows hide logic
acceptance_criteria: auth.ts and init.ts use execFileSync with argument arrays for attrib.
No execSync(string) remains for attrib.
Regression tests cover paths containing quotes or shell metacharacters.

tasks.title: Harden release script against command injection
acceptance_criteria: scripts/release.js uses argument-based command execution helpers.
Version and release tag are validated before command use.
Git, tar, PowerShell, and npm calls avoid shell interpolation.

tasks.title: Minimize npm token leak risk during release
acceptance_criteria: Temporary npm config is isolated or passed via npm-supported env/config options.
Cleanup runs in finally.
No token remains in packages/pros-cli/.npmrc after publish failure.

tasks.title: Implement zip-slip protection
acceptance_criteria: Archive extraction validates target paths against outputDir.
Relative traversal and absolute archive entries are rejected.
Regression test proves malicious archive cannot write outside outputDir.

tasks.title: Make Gitea network access robust
acceptance_criteria: Release fetch and asset download use bounded timeouts.
Release API pagination is handled for tag lookup/latest stable release.
Asset download streams to disk instead of buffering the full response.

tasks.title: Make CLI token entry safer
acceptance_criteria: pros auth token set accepts token from stdin or prompt.
Direct token argument is deprecated or emits a safety warning.
Tests cover the non-argv token path.

tasks.title: Improve install/update robustness
acceptance_criteria: Staging directory is unique per run.
Cleanup runs in finally for all init/update paths.
Version comparison handles or rejects pre-release suffixes deterministically.

tasks.title: Tighten workspace and state validation
acceptance_criteria: workspace.ts uses path.relative for relative paths.
Symlink traversal outside the workspace is blocked or explicitly documented.
doctor.ts validates state.json shape before reporting installed state.

tasks.title: Harden CI release pipeline
acceptance_criteria: Action pinning is tightened to commit SHAs or documented as accepted tech debt.
Windows verification for platform-specific paths is added or explicitly deferred.
Dry-run behavior remains available.

tasks.title: Run regression and verification suite
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes.
npm run typecheck passes.
npm run lint passes.
npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities.
npm run release:dry-run passes.

done_when: All HIGH findings from the QA report are resolved.
All P0 tasks include regression tests.
No shell string interpolation remains for user- or package-influenced values.
Archive extraction cannot write outside the destination directory.
Tokens are not unnecessarily exposed through argv or persistent .npmrc files.
npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm audit, and npm run release:dry-run pass.
